Why did the Late Bronze Age collapse happen?

The Late Bronze Age collapse was caused by a combination of factors, including overexploitation of resources, environmental degradation, and conflicts among city-states. These factors led to economic decline, social unrest, and ultimately the collapse of the Minoan and Mycenaean civilizations.

The Late Bronze Age collapse was caused by a combination of factors, including overexploitation of resources, environmental degradation, and conflicts among city-states. This collapse is documented in the archaeological record and is associated with the decline of the Minoan and Mycenaean civilizations in the Mediterranean. The event is also discussed in historical texts like "The Year Civilization Collapsed" by Eric H. Cline.
